preseason_hypothesis: Jadarian Price wins enough early-down and explosive work to be the highest-upside Seattle back by Week 1
confirming_evidence: Price gets first-team early-down work and designed touches while holding up in protection. WEEK 1 MEASURED: Price led the backfield in snaps (24 of 50), carries (10 of 22) and yards (52, 5.2 avg, long 13) and took both running-back targets.
disconfirming_evidence: Holani or Wilson leads first-team work or Charbonnet returns immediately to starter usage. WEEK 1 CHALLENGES THE HYPOTHESIS: Holani played 23 snaps to Price's 24 — a ONE-SNAP difference — and took 8 carries to Price's 10. This is a near-even committee, not the lead-back workload the hypothesis requires. Wilson played 3 snaps.
review_trigger: Week 2 at Arizona: whether the near-even split holds against a second opponent, and whether either back separates on passing downs. INSIDE-FIVE UNRESOLVED AND UNTESTED: Seattle ran ZERO goal-to-go snaps in Week 1 and no back carried inside the New England 10, so no scoring-role evidence exists. Charbonnet is eligible to return from reserve/PUP after Week 4.

preseason_hypothesis: Shaheed's first full offseason turns him into a larger route-share receiver without removing all return value
confirming_evidence: Shaheed runs with the first-team offense and remains listed at PR/KR. WEEK 1: played 33 of 50 snaps (66%), fourth among pass catchers, and retained return work (1 punt return for 9 yards, 3 kickoff returns for 80).
disconfirming_evidence: Shaheed remains mostly a rotational deep threat or Seattle removes him from return work. WEEK 1 LEANS DISCONFIRMING ON VOLUME: 3 targets and 1 reception for 4 yards, against Smith-Njigba's 11 targets and 122 yards, in a game where Horton was inactive and the room was already thin. He kept the return job.
review_trigger: Week 2 route participation and targets, read against the quarterback situation rather than against the full-game base: Lock threw 22 of Seattle's 24 targets in Week 1.

preseason_hypothesis: AJ Barner remains TE1 but route value depends on Fleury's tight-end deployment
confirming_evidence: Barner plays starter snaps and runs routes in first-team drives. PREMISE CORRECTED 2026-09-10: this hypothesis previously required Barner to run routes 'with Darnold in first-team drives'. Darnold played 5 of 50 snaps before injury, so that condition is untestable as written and the quarterback reference is removed. WEEK 1: Barner played 44 of 50 snaps (88%), second among all pass catchers.
disconfirming_evidence: Barner primarily blocks while Saubert, Arroyo or Kallerup dilute routes. WEEK 1 PARTIAL SIGNAL: a very high 88% snap share produced only 2 targets and 13 yards. Arroyo played 11 snaps (22%) and Saubert 10 (20%), so the room did not dilute him — but high snaps with low targets is the blocking-heavy pattern the hypothesis warns about. No route counts exist to separate the two.
review_trigger: Week 2 tight-end snap and target split. NOT CLOSABLE ON ROUTES: no registered source supplies route counts, so 'route value' can only be approached through snap share and targets.

preseason_hypothesis: Returning all five starters keeps the quarterback's efficiency floor intact
confirming_evidence: Cross, Zabel, Sundell, Bradford and Lucas stay healthy and cohesive. WEEK 1: all five played 50 of 50 offensive snaps. Seattle allowed 2 sacks for 12 yards on 24 attempts.
disconfirming_evidence: Injuries or pass-protection leakage force multiple line changes. WEEK 1 CAVEAT: Darnold was injured on a sack on the opening possession. One sack is not a protection verdict, and no pressure charting exists for Seattle.
review_trigger: First two regular-season games: chart protection exchanges and interior pressure. PREMISE CORRECTED 2026-09-10: this hypothesis was framed as protecting 'Darnold's efficiency floor'. Darnold played 5 snaps before injury and has no prognosis, so the hypothesis is restated around whichever quarterback plays. Returning starters are a personnel baseline, not individual pass-block grades.
